# Report a dead bird

Description: Help us track West Nile virus by reporting dead birds through the state system.

## What to know

Callout: Do not touch dead birds. Wear gloves or use a shovel if you must move them.

Section heading: We collect birds from May through October
Section body: San Francisco collects dead birds during mosquito season to test for West Nile virus and other diseases.

Section heading: We accept all birds except pigeons
Section body: Report crows, jays, hawks, owls, finches, sparrows, and other birds. Do not report pigeons - they do not carry the diseases we test for.

Section heading: Do not report birds that are obviously injured
Section body: If you see obvious trauma like car strikes or cat attacks, the bird probably did not die from disease. Focus on birds that appear to have died without obvious cause.

## What to do

Section heading: Report online to the California Department of Public Health
Section body: Use the state's online system to report your dead bird. They will coordinate with our San Francisco team for pickup and testing.

Button link: Report to CDPH West Nile virus system [External link to CDPH WNV reporting system]

Section heading: Prepare the bird safely for pickup
Section body: Place the bird in a plastic bag using gloves or a shovel. Put the bagged bird in a second bag. Keep it cool and out of direct sunlight until pickup.

Section heading: Questions about dead bird pickup
Section body: Contact HHVC with any questions about the dead bird collection process or testing.

## Related
- Learn how to stop mosquitoes
- Contact HHVC

INTEGRATION NOTES:
- Tagging this Transaction page to HHVC Topic will surface it on the HHVC hub under Vector Services
- External link to CDPH West Nile virus reporting system needs to be verified and maintained
- Collection months (May-October) and bird acceptance criteria should be verified with SFDPH vector control program
- May need coordination with Animal Control Services for collection logistics
- Removed 311 reference per user request and directed questions to HHVC contact instead
